# dlgskill


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

**Workflow.** Start with
[`summary_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#summary_dlg)
unless reading the full dialog, then
[`find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#find_msgs)
or `view_dlg(incl_out=True)` for code, prose, and outputs. Before
editing, read `nbdev.skill` and `exhash.skill`; for cross-notebook
searches, read `rgapi.skill` (`nbrg`).

Use message operations for dialogs and
[`fastcore.nbio.Notebook`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/nbio.html#notebook)/`NbCell`
operations for plain notebooks. Diagnose with `validate_nb`,
`validate_cell`, or `read_nb`. Raw text is only for unparseable files.
Propose missing structural operations; never splice notebook JSON.

View fresh
[`lnhashview_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#lnhashview_msg)/`lnhashview_cell`
addresses before hash-verified edits. Use plain `msg_*` editors where
exhash cannot express the operation. Use structural
[`find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#find_msgs)
predicates for Python symbols/ASTs. Read neighboring prose, including
with `ids=`.

Call documented APIs without speculative fallbacks. Display results
bare, never slice or reformat their reprs. Review returned diffs and
call `dlg.validate()`.

**Files and held objects.** File functions take `dlg=path`, defaulting
to `set_dlg(path)`. Each call rereads; edits save automatically. Methods
edit held objects until `dlg.save()`. Save before switching to file
functions; reopen before resuming methods. Drop address arguments:
`msg_str_replace(id, ..., dlg=p)` becomes `m.str_replace(...)`. Use
`d.mk_message`/`d.remove_msgs` in memory. `Dialog(msgs)` wraps a message
list; `m.dlg` retains ownership.

**Views and identity.** Summaries use `id:t[directives]:content`:
c=code, n=note, p=prompt, r=raw. Replies follow `>`; truncations end
with a bracketed missing-character count. Directives are nbdev metadata,
as in nbio summaries. XML uses `item2xml`, `<out>` replies, and
directive attributes such as bare `export`.

File searches return
[`MsgRows`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgrows)/[`MsgRow`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgrow)
snapshots (`id`, `msg_type`, `content`, `out`, `meta`); method searches
return live
[`FoundMsgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#foundmsgs).
Index by exact id or unique prefix, never position. Context rows use `-`
instead of the first `:`. Default context is one neighbor each side,
including with `ids=`; `headers_only` defaults to zero.

**Placement and metadata.** The host calls
[`set_cur_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_cur_msg);
writes never move it. Unanchored adds follow it, or append if
unset/missing. Chain explicit `after=` anchors for successive additions.

`m.exported` and `only_exp` include source and metadata directives;
assignable `m.meta_exported` uses metadata only.
[`Message.update`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.update)/[`update_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#update_msg)
replace attributes, including whole `meta`; `mergemeta` deep-merges,
with `None` deleting keys. `export=True` adds and `False` removes,
migrating source export to metadata without a negative directive. Diffs
show XML and `meta:`. Text editors’ `out=True` edits prompt replies
only; assign other outputs through `m.output`.

**Kernel execution.** `%nbrun` runs in the current kernel.
[`Dialog.execute`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog.execute)/[`Message.execute`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message.execute)
capture outputs on held messages and return
[`RunResult`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#runresult)
(abbreviated successes, exceptions on failure). They block; use
`asyncio.to_thread` in async hosts. Read
[`Dialog.execute`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog.execute)
for selection, shell lifetime, and saving.

`%%add_msg [dlg] [msg_type] [export] [before=<id>|after=<id>]` takes an
unquoted body, trimming trailing newlines. Keywords override bare
tokens.

`%nbrun [IDS/FLAGS] [fname=PATH]` accepts `above`, `below`, `all`,
`exported`, `ignore_eval`, `continue_on_error`, and `show`. `fname`
overrides
[`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg);
no selection runs all participating code cells. Only explicit ids
display outputs unless `show`. Errors always name the cell; the final
`nbrun: N cells ok` includes any failure count. Execution uses the
kernel’s namespace and standard output/error handling. The magic returns
a coroutine for the host to await.

``` python
from fastcore.test import *
from fastcore.tools import lnhash
from tempfile import mkdtemp
from contextlib import chdir
from IPython.core.interactiveshell import InteractiveShell
```

### set_dlg

``` python
def set_dlg(
    fname, # ipynb path that later calls will default to
    cls:NoneType=None, # `Dialog` subclass to read with from now on (None: keep current; initially `Dialog`)
):
```

*Set the current dialog file, used by these functions when `dlg` is
None*

A host calls
[`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg)
to set the current file and
[`set_cur_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_cur_msg)
to set the current message within it. Solveit sets the message when
running it. An
[`add_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#add_msg)
call without explicit placement then inserts after the prompt receiving
the answer. Writes never move the current message. Calling
[`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg)
clears it because message ids belong to a file. An unset or deleted
current message makes
[`add_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#add_msg)
append instead.

Pass `cls` to
[`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg)
to choose the
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
subclass for subsequent file reads. A host can use this subclass with
its own message fields from `meta_attrs`. The class setting survives
later
[`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg)
calls until you replace it, including when switching files.

[`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg)
expands `~` and resolves an absolute path immediately. Changing
directories, including with `%cd`, does not change the current file.

You can read the stored id and path as `dlgskill.cur_msgid` and
`dlgskill.cur_dlg_path`. Do not import these attributes with
`from ... import`. The setters rebind them, which leaves an imported
binding with an old value. For this reason, `__all__` does not include
them.

### Dialog.msg

``` python
def msg(
    id, # A `Message` (matched by its id), or an id: exact, or unique prefix
):
```

*The matching
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)
in this dialog*

`msg` accepts a message object, an exact id, or a unique id prefix. Use
the id stored in the notebook. It does not remove host display prefixes
such as Solveit’s leading underscore.

The examples use a temporary dialog file. File-based calls will read it
again on each call:

``` python
tdir = Path(mkdtemp())
d = Dialog(name='demo')
setup = d.mk_message('# Setup', msg_type=snote)
calc = d.mk_message('x = 21\nx*2', msg_type=scode, output=code_output('42'))
ask = d.mk_message('Double it.', msg_type=sprompt, output='It is **42**.')
bad = d.mk_message('1/0', msg_type=scode, output=[dict(output_type='error', ename='E', evalue='boom', traceback=['tb'])])
write_ipynb(d, tdir/'demo.ipynb')
test_eq(d.msg(calc.id), calc)
test_eq(d.msg(calc.id[:5]), calc)  # unique prefixes work too
with expect_fail(KeyError, 'no message'): d.msg('zzzz')
```

``` python
def view_msg(
    id, # Message id, looked up in `dlg` (unique prefixes allowed)
    dlg:NoneType=None, # An ipynb path (expands `~`); the current dialog file if None
    nums:bool=True, # Show line numbers?
    start_line:int=1, # Starting line to view
    end_line:int=None, # End line (defaults to last line if None; -1 for EOF)
    lnhashs:bool=False, # Show exhash `lineno|hash|` addresses instead of line numbers?

    trunc_out:bool=True, # Truncate an included output to ~512 chars?
):
```

*Show a message’s content with optional line numbers or exhash
addresses*

``` python
test_eq(str(calc.view()), '1: x = 21\n2: x*2')
test_eq(str(calc.view(start_line=2)), '2: x*2')
test_eq(str(calc.view(lnhashs=True)), f'{lnhash(1, "x = 21")}x = 21\n{lnhash(2, "x*2")}x*2')
assert str(view_msgs(setup.id, calc.id, dlg=tdir/'demo.ipynb', nums=False)).startswith(f"# msg {setup.id}")
test_eq(str(view_msgs(calc.id, dlg=tdir/'demo.ipynb', start_line=2)), f'# msg {calc.id}\n2: x*2')
test_eq(str(calc.view(incl_out=True)), '1: x = 21\n2: x*2\n<out>\n42\n</out>')
assert 'It is **42**.' in str(ask.view(nums=False, incl_out=True))
assert '<out>' not in str(calc.view())
assert '<out>' in str(view_msg(calc.id, dlg=tdir/'demo.ipynb', incl_out=True))
test_eq(str(view_msgs(calc.id, ask.id, dlg=tdir/'demo.ipynb', incl_out=True)).count('<out>'), 2)
```

## Searching

A search result can include both matches and the messages that explain
them.
[`find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#find_msgs)
includes one neighbor on each side by default, even when filtering by
`ids`.

Index results with a message id or unique prefix that you read from the
result. Integer indexing raises an error: position zero could contain
context rather than the match you wanted. Missing or ambiguous ids also
raise errors.

### find_msgs

``` python
def find_msgs(
    re_pattern:str='', # Regex over content (a prompt's reply included), DOTALL+MULTILINE; an invalid regex matches literally
    dlg:NoneType=None, # An ipynb path (expands `~`); the current dialog file if None
    *, msg_type:str=None, # Optional limit by type ('code', 'note', 'prompt', or 'raw')
    only_err:bool=False, # Only code messages with error outputs?
    only_exp:bool=False, # Only exported messages (nbdev export directive in content or meta)?
    ids:str='', # Optionally filter by ids (comma-separated str, or list); results are always in dialog order, whatever order the ids are given
    before:int=0, # Also include n messages before each match
    after:int=0, # Also include n messages after each match
    context:int=None, # Messages of context around matches (default 1, or 0 when `headers_only`)
    limit:int=None, # Max matched messages
    use_case:bool=False, # Case-sensitive matching?
    use_regex:bool=True, # Regex matching (else plain substring)?
    headers_only:bool=False, # Only heading notes (an outline view)?
    header_section:str=None, # Return the section starting with this heading, plus its children
    pred:<built-in function callable>=None, # Extra match criterion, e.g. from `symdef_finder`/`symref_finder`/`ast_finder`, or host-specific flags
)->aidialog.dialog.MsgRows: # Snapshot rows (`id`, `msg_type`, `content`, `out`, `meta`), indexed by id and shown as previews with context rows marked
```

*Find messages in the dialog file matching all the given criteria; for
live results, call
[`Dialog.find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#dialog.find_msgs)*

### Dialog.find_msgs

``` python
def find_msgs(
    re_pattern:str='', # Regex over content (a prompt's reply included), DOTALL+MULTILINE; an invalid regex matches literally
    msg_type:str=None, # Optional limit by type ('code', 'note', 'prompt', or 'raw')
    only_err:bool=False, # Only code messages with error outputs?
    only_exp:bool=False, # Only exported messages (nbdev export directive in content or meta)?
    ids:str='', # Optionally filter by ids (comma-separated str, or list); results are always in dialog order, whatever order the ids are given
    before:int=0, # Also include n messages before each match
    after:int=0, # Also include n messages after each match
    context:int=None, # Messages of context around matches (default 1, or 0 when `headers_only`)
    limit:int=None, # Max matched messages
    use_case:bool=False, # Case-sensitive matching?
    use_regex:bool=True, # Regex matching (else plain substring)?
    headers_only:bool=False, # Only heading notes (an outline view)?
    header_section:str=None, # Return the section starting with this heading, plus its children
    pred:<built-in function callable>=None, # Extra match criterion, e.g. from `symdef_finder`/`symref_finder`/`ast_finder`, or host-specific flags
)->__main__.FoundMsgs: # Live messages plus context rows, indexed by id, so results can be edited directly
```

*Find this dialog’s messages matching all the given criteria*

[`Dialog.find_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#dialog.find_msgs)
returns live messages. Edits through its result change the held dialog.
You can search an existing message list by wrapping it in
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
without changing the messages’ owners.

Search text matches a prompt’s request or reply. An invalid regular
expression falls back to literal matching, allowing search text from
users to include characters such as `*`. Pass `pred` for another
criterion, such as a host-specific flag.

Use `header_section` for a section beginning at a note heading. Use
`headers_only` for an outline. Outline searches default to no context.
Other searches default to one message on each side. Pass `context=0` for
exact matches only:

``` python
test_eq(d.find_msgs('42', context=0), [ask])  # matches the reply text
test_eq(d.find_msgs(r'x\*2', msg_type=scode, context=0), [calc])
test_eq(d.find_msgs(only_err=True, context=0), [bad])
test_eq(len(d.find_msgs(r'x\*2')), 3)  # context defaults to 1: the match plus both neighbours
test_eq(d.find_msgs(headers_only=True), [setup])
test_eq(d.find_msgs(header_section='Setup', context=0), list(d.messages))  # everything under the heading
test_eq(Dialog(d.messages[:3]).find_msgs('42', context=0), [ask])  # an ephemeral wrap makes any message list searchable
fm = d.find_msgs('42', context=0)
fm[ask.id].content = 'Double it, please.'
test_eq(ask.content, 'Double it, please.')  # live objects: the edit landed on the dialog
assert ask.dlg is d  # ...and the wrap above didn't steal the message from its real dialog
test_eq(d.find_msgs('*42*', context=0), [ask])  # an invalid regex falls back to a literal match
test_eq(d.find_msgs(pred=lambda m: m.msg_type==sprompt, context=0), [ask])  # host-specific extra criterion
xd = Dialog(name='exports')
exp1 = xd.mk_message('#| export\ndef f(): pass', msg_type=scode)
exp2 = xd.mk_message('def g(): pass', msg_type=scode)
exp2.meta_exported = True
deep = xd.mk_message('## Deep\nbody under the heading', msg_type=snote)
test_eq(xd.find_msgs(only_exp=True, context=0), [exp1, exp2])
test_eq(xd.find_msgs(header_section='Deep', context=0), [deep])  # matched on the first line only
test_eq(xd.find_msgs(header_section='## Deep', context=0), [deep])  # a '#'-prefixed argument pins the level
test_eq(xd.find_msgs(header_section='# Deep', context=0), [])
```

A query by `ids` still includes neighboring messages. The
integer-indexing error suggests an id from the actual matches:

``` python
fm = d.find_msgs(ids=calc.id)
test_eq((fm.matched, len(fm)), ({calc.id}, 3))
with expect_fail(TypeError, 'context rows'): fm[0]
test_eq(fm[calc.id], calc)
fm
```

    b73e2cdc:n-# Setup
    1b68e089:c:x = 21¶x*2 ⇒ out(103)
    701cf781:p-Double it, please.
    > It is **42**.

The file function returns
[`MsgRow`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgrow)
snapshots, not live messages. Use their ids for subsequent edits. We
saved the file before changing `ask` in memory above. This search
therefore returns its earlier content:

``` python
rows = find_msgs('42', dlg=tdir/'demo.ipynb', context=0)
test_eq([r.id for r in rows], [ask.id])
test_eq(rows[ask.id].content, 'Double it.')  # the file's snapshot, not the live edit above
assert not isinstance(rows[ask.id], Message) and rows[ask.id].msg_type==sprompt
with expect_fail(TypeError, 'path'): find_msgs('42', dlg=d)  # a live Dialog goes through the method, never dlg=
rows
```

    701cf781:p:Double it.
    > It is **42**.

### Message.split

``` python
def split(
    *linenos:int, # Split before each of these 1-based lines

```

*Split this message into pieces (returned as
[`Msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#msgs); the
first keeps its id): one `'\n\n'` is absorbed at each cut (so
[`merge_msgs`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#merge_msgs)
restores blank-line-separated content byte-exactly), `meta_attrs`
fields, the cell `meta`, and a leading `#| export` copy to every piece,
attachments follow their references, and unreferenced ones stay on the
first piece*

``` python
sd = Dialog(name='s')
sm = sd.mk_message('#| export\ndef f(): pass\ndef g(): pass', msg_type=scode, meta={'k': 1})
i1,i2 = sm.split(3)
test_eq([m.content for m in sd.messages], ['#| export\ndef f(): pass', '#| export\ndef g(): pass'])
test_eq([m.meta for m in sd.messages], [{'k': 1}, {'k': 1}])  # whole cell meta copies to every piece
i2.meta['k'] = 2  # pieces don't share the dict
test_eq(i1.meta, {'k': 1})
sd.merge_msgs(i1, i2)
test_eq((sd.messages[0].content, sd.messages[0].meta), ('#| export\ndef f(): pass\n\ndef g(): pass', {'k': 1}))
hd = Dialog(name='hoist')
h1, h2 = hd.mk_message('def a(): pass'), hd.mk_message('#| export\ndef b(): pass')
hm = hd.merge_msgs(h1, h2)  # any exported piece exports the merge, via meta
test_eq((hm.content, hm.meta, hm.exported), ('def a(): pass\n\ndef b(): pass', {'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}}, True))
sd.mk_message('tail', msg_type=snote)
sd.move_msgs(i1, after=sd.messages[-1])
test_eq([m.content[:4] for m in sd.messages], ['tail', '#| e'])
```

``` python
ad = Dialog(name='atts')
at1, at2 = Attachment(b'x', 'text/plain'), Attachment(b'y', 'text/plain')
am = ad.mk_message(f'see attachment:{at1.id}\nplain tail', msg_type=snote, attachments=[at1, at2])
p1, p2 = am.split(2)
test_eq(len(p1.attachments), 2)  # the referenced one, plus the unreferenced one kept on the first piece
test_eq(p2.attachments, [])
jd = Dialog(name='junction')
j = jd.mk_message('a\n\n\nb', msg_type=snote)
j1, j2 = j.split(4)
test_eq((j1.content, j2.content), ('a\n', 'b'))  # one '\n\n' absorbed at the cut: exactly what merge re-inserts
test_eq(jd.merge_msgs(j1, j2).content, 'a\n\n\nb')  # ...so blank-line-separated content round trips byte-exactly
k1, k2 = jd.mk_message('a\n\nb', msg_type=snote).split(3)
test_eq((k1.content, k2.content), ('a', 'b'))
w1, w2 = jd.mk_message('a\n\n\nb', msg_type=snote).split(3)  # cut on the blank line: residue stays on the right
test_eq((w1.content, w2.content), ('a', '\nb'))
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'Exactly one'): jd.move_msgs(w2)
```

## Editing message text

The text editors use `fastcore.tools` operations on message content. Set
`out=True` to edit a prompt’s reply Markdown instead. Assignment
converts the edited reply back to an output list with
[`prompt_output`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#prompt_output).

Other message types do not support text edits to outputs. Assign a code
message’s `output` directly. Prompt requests and replies are separate
editing targets. The former behavior that joined them for editing is no
longer supported.

Pass a list of ids or `'all'` for a bulk edit. The result omits
unchanged messages and includes errors.

The editors inherit their signatures from `fastcore.tools`. `doc()`
groups six shared replacement options under `replace_params`, matching
`fastcore.editskill`:

``` python
(tdir/'edit.ipynb').write_bytes((tdir/'demo.ipynb').read_bytes())  # scratch copy: demo.ipynb stays pristine for later sections
with chdir(tdir): set_dlg('edit.ipynb')
test_eq(cur_dlg_path, (tdir/'edit.ipynb').resolve())
test_eq(cur_dlg().msg(calc.id).content, 'x = 21\nx*2')
diff = msg_str_replace(calc.id, 'x = 21', 'x = 40')
assert '-x = 21' in str(diff) and '+x = 40' in str(diff)
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'edit.ipynb').msg(calc.id).content, 'x = 40\nx*2')
```

``` python
diff = msg_str_replace(ask.id, '**42**', '**80**', out=True)
assert '+It is **80**.' in str(diff)
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'edit.ipynb').msg(ask.id).ai_res, 'It is **80**.')
assert str(msg_str_replace(calc.id, "'42'", "'80'", out=True)).startswith('error:')
assert str(msg_del_lines(setup.id, 1, 1, out=True)).startswith('error:')
bulk = msg_str_replace([setup.id, bad.id], '1/0', 'pass')
test_eq(len(bulk), 2)  # bulk mode reports errors alongside diffs
assert 'error' in bulk[0][1] and '+pass' in bulk[1][1]
```

## Structural search

Searching for `cfg =` misses a binding such as `cfg, aux = load()`. A
broad text search for a short name also finds unrelated text. Use
remold’s structural queries through `find_msgs(pred=...)` for Python
symbols and syntax.

[`symdef_finder`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#symdef_finder)
finds top-level bindings. These include tuple unpacking, `for`,
`with ... as`, walrus expressions, imports, and `def` or `class`
definitions.
[`symref_finder`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#symref_finder)
finds references to a name.
[`ast_finder`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#ast_finder)
matches an ast-grep pattern.

The name queries return no matches for content that cannot parse as
Python. This excludes ordinary prose in the example below:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dlgskill.py#L460"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

`remold`)*

``` python
fd = Dialog(name='finders')
f1 = fd.mk_message('cfg, aux = load_cfg()', msg_type=scode)
f2 = fd.mk_message('print(render(cfg))', msg_type=scode)
fd.mk_message('cfg is set up above', msg_type=snote)
test_eq(fd.find_msgs(pred=symdef_finder('cfg'), context=0), [f1])
test_eq(fd.find_msgs(pred=symref_finder('cfg'), context=0), [f2])
test_eq(fd.find_msgs(pred=ast_finder('render($_)'), context=0), [f2])
```

## Hash-verified edits

Call `m.lnhashview()` to read a held message with exhash addresses. Use
those addresses in `m.exhash()` to edit it. Exhash rejects stale
addressed text.

[`Message.lnhashview`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#message.lnhashview)
calls `view(lnhashs=True)` and accepts its `start_line` and `end_line`
range. For a file, use
[`lnhashview_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#lnhashview_msg)
and
[`msg_exhash`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#msg_exhash)
with an id and `dlg` path. The edit functions import exhash when you
call them. The rest of aidialog does not require it:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dlgskill.py#L494"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
diff = calc.exhash((lnhash(1, 'x = 21'), 's', '21', '12'))
```

Like
[`view_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#view_msg),
these file functions resolve an id in `dlg`, or in the current file when
`dlg` is `None`.
[`msg_exhash`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#msg_exhash)
saves its edit automatically:

``` python
msg_replace_lines(calc.id, new_content='a = 1\na*2')
test_eq(str(lnhashview_msg(calc.id, start_line=2, end_line=2)), f'{lnhash(2, "a*2")}a*2')
diff = msg_exhash(calc.id, (lnhash(1, 'a = 1'), 's', '1', '9'))
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'edit.ipynb').msg(calc.id).content, 'a = 9\na*2')
```

## Working with dialog files

Pass an `.ipynb` path as `dlg` to a file function. Leave it as `None` to
use the current file from
[`set_dlg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#set_dlg).
Each call reads the file again. Mutating calls save their changes.

For a held
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog),
call its methods instead of passing it as `dlg`. Methods edit in memory
until `dlg.save()`.
[`cur_dlg()`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#cur_dlg)
reads the current file into a new held object.

Use one approach at a time for each file. Save held edits before using
file functions. Reopen the dialog afterward to see file changes in
memory. After aidialog has normalized a file, saving an unchanged dialog
preserves its serialized bytes. The functions below create, edit, and
delete messages directly in files:

``` python
set_dlg(tdir/'demo.ipynb')
assert '<prompt' in str(view_dlg())
assert str(summary_dlg()).count('\n')==4  # 4 messages, plus the prompt's reply line
s = str(find_msgs(r'x\*2', msg_type=scode, context=0))
assert s and s.count('\n')==0  # a code row is one preview line (empty would pass a bare count check)
xd.mk_message('', msg_type=sraw, meta=dict(rec_kind='system', rec={}))
assert 'kind="system"' in str(xd.view())  # tagged raws are badged, never shown as ordinary content
```

A missing `dlg` file raises `FileNotFoundError`:

``` python
with expect_fail(FileNotFoundError, 'does not exist'): summary_dlg(tdir/'missing.ipynb')
```

``` python
nm = add_msg('print(9)', after=calc.id)
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(nm).content, 'print(9)')
test_eq(del_msgs(nm)[0].content, 'print(9)')
with expect_fail(KeyError, 'no message'): read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(nm)
nd = create_dlg(tdir/'new.ipynb', '# hi', 'note')
test_eq(nd.messages[0].msg_type, snote)
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'new.ipynb').msg(nd.messages[0]).content, '# hi')
```

Pass a host’s
[`Dialog`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#dialog)
subclass with `set_dlg(cls=...)` to use it for later file reads. Here
its
[`Message`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dialog.html#message)
subclass exposes another metadata field as an attribute:

``` python
class _HostMsg(Message):
    meta_attrs = dict(Message.meta_attrs, starred='starred')
class _HostDlg(Dialog): msg_cls = _HostMsg

set_dlg(tdir/'demo.ipynb', cls=_HostDlg)
starred = add_msg('to star', 'note', meta=dict(starred=True))
assert cur_dlg().msg(starred.id).starred  # promoted to an attribute by the host class
set_dlg(tdir/'demo.ipynb')  # bare set_dlg keeps the class...
assert isinstance(cur_dlg(), _HostDlg)
set_dlg(tdir/'demo.ipynb', cls=Dialog)  # ...replacing it is explicit
assert not isinstance(cur_dlg(), _HostDlg)
del_msgs(starred)
```

    cf6e6ad3:n:to star

An
[`add_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#add_msg)
without placement inserts after the current message. Pass each new
message as the next call’s `after` argument to keep additions in order.
Writing does not move the current message:

``` python
set_cur_msg(calc)
a = add_msg('a = 1')
b = add_msg('b = 2', after=a)
test_eq(cur_msg().id, calc.id)
test_eq(cur_msgid, calc.id)  # the bare state: importers read it as `dlgskill.cur_msgid`
summary_dlg()
```

    b73e2cdc:n:# Setup
    1b68e089:c:x = 21¶x*2 ⇒ out(103)
    ff2ddd57:c:a = 1
    466690d7:c:b = 2
    701cf781:p:Double it.
    > It is **42**.
    88b899da:c:1/0 ⇒ out(79)

If the current message no longer exists,
[`add_msg`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#add_msg)
appends. Deleting it does not make the next unanchored addition fail:

``` python
set_cur_msg('gone')
z = add_msg('z = 3')
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').messages[-1].content, 'z = 3')
del_msgs(a, b, z)
set_cur_msg(None)
summary_dlg()
```

    b73e2cdc:n:# Setup
    1b68e089:c:x = 21¶x*2 ⇒ out(103)
    701cf781:p:Double it.
    > It is **42**.
    88b899da:c:1/0 ⇒ out(79)

Set `export=True` to add the nbdev export flag to metadata. You can also
supply it in `meta`. The summary marks the new message with `[export]`:

``` python
xm = add_msg('def q(): pass', after=calc.id, export=True)
test_eq(xm.meta, {'nbdev': {'export': 'true'}})
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(xm).meta_exported, True)
assert ':c[export]:' in xm.preview()
del_msgs(xm)
```

applies

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
    id, # A `Message`, or an id: exact, or unique prefix
    dlg:NoneType=None, # An ipynb path (expands `~`); the current dialog file if None
    *, mergemeta:dict=None, # `deep_merge` into `meta`; a `None` value deletes its key
```

The diff includes a `meta:` line for metadata that the XML does not
show. nbdev directives also affect XML attributes, as these export
changes demonstrate:

``` python
set_dlg(tdir/'demo.ipynb')
print(update_msg(calc.id, export=True))
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(calc.id).meta_exported, True)
print(update_msg(calc.id, mergemeta=dict(nbdev=None)))
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(calc.id).exported, False)
```

In IPython, write a new message with
`%%add_msg [<path>] before=<id>|after=<id> [code|note|prompt|raw] [export]`.
The cell body needs no Python quoting. The magic removes trailing
newlines from it. You can use `dlg=` and `msg_type=` instead of bare
tokens. Keywords take precedence:

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dlgskill.py#L565"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### add_msg_magic

``` python
def add_msg_magic(
    line, cell
):
```

*Add the magic body as a message, trimming trailing newlines; `export`
sets the metadata export flag.*

``` python
nm = add_msg_magic(f"note dlg={tdir/'demo.ipynb'} after={calc.id}", 'magic body')
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(nm.id).content, 'magic body')
test_eq(nm.msg_type, 'note')
xm = add_msg_magic(f"code export dlg={tdir/'demo.ipynb'} after={calc.id}", 'def r(): pass')
test_eq(read_ipynb(tdir/'demo.ipynb').msg(xm.id).meta_exported, True)
```

`%nbrun` runs notebook code in the current kernel. Give cell ids or
unique prefixes to select cells. The bare flags are `above`, `below`,
`all`, `exported`, `ignore_eval`, `continue_on_error`, and `show`. As
with `%%add_msg`, `k=v` keywords take precedence over bare tokens.
Without a selection, it runs all participating code cells. `fname`
selects a different file for one call.

Explicit id selections run through
[`fastcore.nbio.run_cell`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/nbio.html#run_cell)
with `store_history=True`. The kernel’s displayhook shows their results.
A trailing semicolon suppresses the result through the kernel’s normal
handling.

Other selected cells run silently. These include the additional cells
selected by `above`, `below`, `all`, and `exported`. The runner captures
their stdout and stderr to keep setup output out of the display. Use
`show` to display every selected cell.

Failures always appear, even in silent runs. Each run ends with
`nbrun: N cells ok`, plus a failure count when needed. The examples
below show stopping at an error and continuing past it.

The runner uses the kernel’s namespace and standard streams, display
publisher, and error display. It does not need host-specific output
handling. The magic returns a coroutine.
[`fastcore.aio.enable_async_magics`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/aio.html#enable_async_magics)
provides the machinery to await it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/aidialog/blob/main/aidialog/dlgskill.py#L599"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
rd = create_dlg(tdir/'run.ipynb', 'zz = 5')
rm2 = add_msg('zz2 = zz+1', after=rd.messages[0].id, dlg=tdir/'run.ipynb')
await nbrun_magic(f"{rm2.id} above fname={tdir/'run.ipynb'}")
```

    nbrun: 1 cell ok

The same loop can run with an `InteractiveShell` and its own namespace:

``` python
psh = InteractiveShell()
await _run_nb_cells(psh, [rm2.id], tdir/'run.ipynb', above=True)
test_eq((psh.user_ns['zz'], psh.user_ns['zz2']), (5, 6))
bad = add_msg('no_such_name', after=rm2.id, dlg=tdir/'run.ipynb')
cap = io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap): await _run_nb_cells(psh, [bad.id], tdir/'run.ipynb')
assert f'nbrun: error in cell {bad.id}' in cap.getvalue() and 'NameError' in cap.getvalue()
```

    nbrun: 2 cells ok

``` python
noisy = add_msg("print('noisy')", after=rm2.id, dlg=tdir/'run.ipynb')
target = add_msg("print('target')", after=noisy.id, dlg=tdir/'run.ipynb')
cap = io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap): await _run_nb_cells(psh, [target.id], tdir/'run.ipynb', above=True)
out = cap.getvalue()
assert 'target' in out and 'noisy' not in out and '---' not in out
assert 'nbrun: 4 cells ok' in out
cap = io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap): await _run_nb_cells(psh, [target.id], tdir/'run.ipynb', above=True, show=True)
assert 'noisy' in cap.getvalue()
cap = io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap): await _run_nb_cells(psh, [], tdir/'run.ipynb', all=True)
allout = cap.getvalue()
assert str(bad.id) in allout and 'noisy' not in allout and 'NameError' in allout
assert 'nbrun: 4 cells ok, 1 failed' in allout
out
```

    'target\nnbrun: 4 cells ok\n'

The runner stops at a failing cell by default. It does not raise the
exception again after the shell displays it. This avoids a duplicate
traceback. A failing silent cell’s captured stdout and stderr appear
before the `nbrun: error in cell` line. Successful silent cells do not
display either stream:

``` python
after_bad = add_msg('should_not_run = 1', after=bad.id, dlg=tdir/'run.ipynb')
warner = add_msg("import sys; sys.stderr.write('warn-noise\\n'); zz3 = 1", after=rm2.id, dlg=tdir/'run.ipynb')
cap, cerr = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap), redirect_stderr(cerr): await _run_nb_cells(psh, [], tdir/'run.ipynb', all=True)
assert 'should_not_run' not in psh.user_ns
assert psh.user_ns['zz3'] == 1 and 'warn-noise' not in cerr.getvalue()
```

`continue_on_error` runs past failures. The summary counts successes and
failures separately:

``` python
cap2 = io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap2): await _run_nb_cells(psh, [], tdir/'run.ipynb', all=True, stop=False)
test_eq(psh.user_ns['should_not_run'], 1)
cap2.getvalue().splitlines()[-1]
```

    'nbrun: 6 cells ok, 1 failed'

With no ids or selection flags,
[`nbrun_magic`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/aidialog/dlgskill.html#nbrun_magic)
selects `all`:

``` python
cap3 = io.StringIO()
with redirect_stdout(cap3): await nbrun_magic(f"fname={tdir/'run.ipynb'}")
assert re.search(r'nbrun: \d+ cells ok', cap3.getvalue())
cap3.getvalue().splitlines()[-1]
```

Bulk selections use the `eval` rules from
[`fastcore.nbio.select_cells`](https://fastcore.fast.ai/nbio.html#select_cells).
A cell-level directive overrides the notebook setting, which overrides
the default. A cell with `#| eval: false` does not participate in bulk
runs. Naming that cell explicitly by id still runs it.

Use `ignore_eval` to bypass this filter. The retired `skip_noeval` flag
raises an error explaining its replacement:

``` python
ed = create_dlg(tdir/'ev.ipynb', 'ran = 1')
en = add_msg('#| eval: false\nnever = 1', after=ed.messages[0].id, dlg=tdir/'ev.ipynb')
await nbrun_magic(f"fname={tdir/'ev.ipynb'}")
assert 'never' not in get_ipython().user_ns              # bulk runs follow the eval cascade
await nbrun_magic(f"ignore_eval fname={tdir/'ev.ipynb'}")
test_eq(never, 1)                                        # ignore_eval: Jupyter-style run-all
with expect_fail(ValueError, 'skip_noeval'): nbrun_magic('skip_noeval')
```

    nbrun: 1 cell ok
    nbrun: 2 cells ok
